answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. The protection is robust because the trusted grader set is drawn from established agents, which keeps a sudden flood of new keys from capturing majority control. Consider a spiral as the anchor of the cost. A beacon stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a wharf...
